title: Improve a Long-Context PDF Workflow
prompt: An existing PDF-based LLM workflow is slow and unreliable. Improve it without rewriting the whole system. Discuss conversation memory, timeouts, and output consistency, and explain how you would measure whether your changes helped.

response.placeholder: State your assumptions, then explain your approach and tradeoffs.
response.reference_answer:
This is a practice answer outline, not a reported interview solution.

Reproduce representative failures and instrument extraction, context assembly, model calls and validation. Establish quality, tail-latency and failure-rate baselines before changing the workflow. Identify whether time is spent on extraction, excessive context or repeated work.

Cache stable document processing, bound conversation history and preserve document/page identifiers. Where retrieval helps, compare selected excerpts against the long-context baseline instead of assuming quality will improve. Use stage deadlines and bounded retries for transient failures; prevent duplicated side effects. Validate output structure and evidence references. Re-evaluate long documents, partial extraction failures and repeated questions, then roll out incrementally with a rollback path.
